{{nihongo|'''Imaki-Aosaka-Inami-Ikegami Shrine'''|今城青坂稲実池上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Imaki Aosaka Inami Ikegami Shrine''' (いまきあおさかいなみいけがみじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located along the {{ill|Kanna River|Q11590491|qid=Q11590491|lt=Kanna River}}, a tributary of the {{ill|Tone River|ar|توني (نهر)|arz|نهر تونى|be|Тонэ|bg|Тоне (река)|ca|Riu Tone|cs|Tone|de|Tone (Fluss)|eo|Tone (rivero)|es|Río Tone|eu|Tone ibaia|fa|تونه‌گاوا|fi|Tonejoki|fr|Tone-gawa|he|טונה (נהר)|hi|टोन नदी|hu|Tone (folyó, Japán)|id|Sungai Tone|it|Tone (fiume)|ja|利根川|ko|도네강|lt|Tonė|nl|Tone (Japanse rivier)|no|Tone (elv)|pl|Tone (rzeka)|pt|Rio Tone|ru|Тоне (река)|simple|Tone River|sv|Tonegawa|th|แม่น้ำโทเนะ|tr|Tone Nehri|uk|Тоне (річка)|vi|Sông Tone (Nhật Bản)|wuu|利根川|zh|利根川|qid=Q177452}}, in Sekiguchi, {{ill|Kamikawa, Saitama|Q1346757|qid=Q1346757}}, {{ill|Kodama District, Saitama|ceb|Kodama-gun|fa|ناحیه کوداما، سایتاما|fr|District de Kodama|id|Distrik Kodama, Saitama|it|Distretto di Kodama|ja|児玉郡|ko|고다마군|pl|Powiat Kodama|ru|Кодама (уезд)|simple|Kodama District, Saitama|th|อำเภอโคดามะ|uk|Повіт Кодама|zh|兒玉郡|qid=Q938038}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. The enshrined deities are Okami no Kami, Toyouke-bime no Mikoto, Mizuhanome no Kami, Haniyasuhime no Mikoto, and Toyoukehime no Mikoto (four deities). {{Citation needed range|It is considered a candidate shrine (ronsha) for the Engishiki-listed “Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine” of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}} {{ill|Kami district|Q11634927|qid=Q11634927}}, and its former shrine rank was village shrine.|date=February 2025}}

=== History ===
In {{ill|Jinki (era)|Q1373210|qid=Q1373210}} Year 1 ({{ill|724|Q23549|qid=Q23549}}),<ref name="郡村誌">“Village Records of Kami District, Musashi Province,” Vol. 2, Sekiguchi Village</ref> the ancestor of the {{ill|Abo clan|Q11450278|qid=Q11450278}} of the {{ill|Tan Party|Q11368483|qid=Q11368483}}, one of the {{ill|Musashi Seven Parties|Q11546323|qid=Q11546323}}, transferred (kanjō) {{ill|Niukawakami Shrine (Q246370)|Q246370|qid=Q246370}} of {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, naming it “Niu Shrine.”<ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒">Shrine noticeboard, “62nd Ise Grand Shrine Shikinen Sengu Commemoration: History of Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine”</ref>

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} Year 5 ({{ill|1577|Q6704|qid=Q6704}}) March, the Sekiguchi area of Abo Village was separated to form Sekiguchi Village. At that time, this shrine was relocated from behind the Rokusho Shrine (present-day {{ill|Abo Shrine|Q85884328|qid=Q85884328|lt=Abo Shrine}}) to Ikegami in Sekiguchi Village, becoming the guardian shrine of Sekiguchi Village.<ref name="神社明細帳">Saitama Prefecture, “Shrine Register” (compiled by Saitama Prefecture, compiled after 1879)</ref>
The origin of the name “Sekiguchi” is said to derive from its location at the weir gate (sekiguchi) of the Abo irrigation canal serving the thirteen villages of the Abo territory.

In the Meiji period, the shrine name was changed from “Niu Myōjin Shrine”<ref name="新編武蔵風土記稿">“Newly Compiled Gazetteer of Musashi Province” (compiled by the Geography Bureau of {{ill|Shoheizaka Academy|Q4059219|qid=Q4059219}}, compiled between 1810 and 1830)</ref> to {{Reliability to be verified range|“Imaki Aoyasaka Inami Ikegami Shrine”|date=February 2025}}.<ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒"/>

=== Events <ref name="今城青八坂稲実池上神社御由緒" /> ===
* New Year Festival (January 2)
* Spring Festival (March 19)
* Kokage Festival (April 23)
* Oshōjin (July 24)
* Autumn Festival (October 19)
* Niiname-sai (December 10)

=== Access ===
* From JR {{ill|Takasaki Line|Q1346657|qid=Q1346657}} {{ill|Honjō Station (Saitama)|Q844906|qid=Q844906}}, take the Asahi Bus bound for “Kanzen General Branch Office” for 20 minutes. Get off at “Tanjō Station Entrance.” 10 minutes on foot.
* From JR {{ill|Hachikō Line|Q1372071|qid=Q1372071}} {{ill|Tanshō Station|id|Stasiun Tanshō|ja|丹荘駅|ko|단쇼역|tl|Estasyon ng Tanshō|ur|ٹانشو اسٹیشن|zh|丹莊站|qid=Q845044}}, 11 minutes on foot (850 m)
